title: Lesson 04 — Scene planning & the plan file

items.prompt: What is the typical length of a single production scene?
options: As long as the full explanation needs.
items.explanation: Scenes run 30–90 s; a 10-minute video is usually 8–14 scenes. One scene per concept, several focused scenes rather than one long staging.

items.prompt: Why write plan.md before any animation code?
options: It forces one concept per scene, visible beats, and deliberate pauses while changes are still cheap.
It is required by the manim CLI to render a scene.
It makes rendering measurably faster at export time.
It replaces the need for run_time and self.wait in code.
items.explanation: The plan catches overloaded scenes, missing reading time, and color drift before code exists. Code then transcribes the plan; rendering speed is unaffected.
The scene may hold mixed mobject types, so cleanup uses Group(*self.mobjects) — never VGroup — then self.wait(0.3) before the next scene.

items.prompt: What total on-screen duration (seconds, one decimal) does this beat plan produce?
items.explanation: Animation time 1.5+0.8+1.5+0.5 = 4.3 s; wait time 1.0+0.8+2.5+0.3 = 4.6 s; total 8.9 s. Waits are screen time too — a beat plan's duration is the sum of both, which is why over-pausing a plan shows up here first.

items.prompt: This scene breaks a planning rule. Find the broken line and choose the fix.
items.code:
self.play(Write(title), run_time=1.5)
self.wait(1.0)
self.play(Create(circle), Create(graph), Write(label), Write(note), run_time=0.8)
self.wait(0.5)
options: Split into separate beats (or cut elements): at most 3–4 competing elements reveal at once.
Increase run_time to 5.0 so everything fits.
items.explanation: Line 3 reveals four elements in one beat — over the 3–4 competing-element budget and hiding which element matters. Split the beats or cut what is not pulling its weight; stretching run_time does not fix attention overload.

items.prompt: Which scene plans pass the self-critique questions? (Select all that pass.)
options: "Show that the minimum of the curve sits on the line" — one sentence, one reveal, 2.5 s hold.
"Explain derivatives, integrate the result, and display the proof" — one sentence, 90 s.
"Pose the puzzle, let the obvious approach fail" — one sentence, part of a mystery arc.
"Display the formula table for reference" — one sentence, no reveal, 10 s.
items.explanation: Passing plans are one sentence AND have a payoff (a reveal/aha). The second crams three concepts into one scene; the fourth presents information with no reveal — cut or merge it.

items.prompt: Write a plan.md and its scene for "a² + b² = c² via three squares on a triangle" (build-up arc). Paste both and self-score.
items.modelAnswer:
# Plan — Pythagoras by area

## Overview
- **Topic:** a^2 + b^2 = c^2 as visible area.
- **Aha:** the two small squares together tile the big one.
- **Arc:** build-up (seed: right triangle -> perturb: erect squares ->
  generalise: the identity -> apply: tile).
- **Grounding:** scene-planning.md.

## Palette
BG #1C1C1C; PRIMARY #58C4DD (a- and b-squares); ACCENT #FFFF00 (c-square).

## Beat table (one scene, ~12 s)
| # | Beat | run_time | wait |
|---|------|---:|---:|
| 1 | Triangle draws | 1.0 | 0.5 |
| 2 | Two small squares erect | 1.2 | 1.0 |
| 3 | Hypotenuse square erects | 1.2 | 1.0 |
| 4 | Small squares tile into big (key aha) | 1.5 | 2.5 |
| 5 | Clean exit | 0.6 | 0.3 |

# Scene (transcribed from the table)
from manim import *

class PythagorasByArea(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#1C1C1C"
        tri = Polygon([-2, -1, 0], [2, -1, 0], [2, 1.5, 0], color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(tri), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(0.5)
        sq_a = Square(side_length=1.5, color="#58C4DD").next_to(tri, LEFT, buff=0)
        sq_b = Square(side_length=1.5, color="#58C4DD").next_to(tri, DOWN, buff=0)
        self.play(LaggedStart(Create(sq_a), Create(sq_b), lag_ratio=0.3), run_time=1.2)
        self.wait(1.0)
        sq_c = Square(side_length=2.1, color="#FFFF00").rotate(0.6435).next_to(tri, UP + RIGHT, buff=0)
        self.play(Create(sq_c), run_time=1.2)
        self.wait(1.0)
        caption = Text("the two tile the one", font_size=28)
        caption.to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.8)
        self.play(Write(caption), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(2.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(Group(*self.mobjects)), run_time=0.6)

rubric.criterion: Plan states arc, palette with color meanings, and a beat table (run_time + wait per beat).
Every scene/beat describable in one sentence — one concept each.
Geometry before algebra: squares tile before any formula appears.
Key aha gets the longest hold (>= 2.0 s); every reveal has a wait.
Color constants with fixed meanings; clean exit via Group(*self.mobjects).

items.explanation: The model shows plan-first discipline: the beat table exists before code, the code transcribes it, and the aha (tiling) gets the longest pause.
